thread:
maria: heads up — customer 'AcmeMaps' reporting 403s from their Dedicated endpoint since last night. Only affects requests routed through their VPC LB.

sam: which error exactly? 401/403 from our side or upstream?

maria: 403 from our inference gateway. The client's logs show a 403 response body: 'missing required scope: inference.request'. They say token is the same that worked earlier this week.

alex: any chance there was a change in their LB or Istio config that strips/rewrites auth headers? We've seen that before with HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1 conversions.

maria: customer says they haven't changed anything. They routed traffic through a new NLB in front of the VPC yesterday for autoscaling.

devin: can we get a repro curl to compare headers? maria, ask them to run from inside their VPC (or provide tcpdump) with verbose curl: 

maria: asked and they returned this minimal repro. Paste below.

maria: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ey...VALID_TOKEN..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://dedicated-123.redwood.example.com/v1/complete \n  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
*** Request header: Authorization: Bearer ey...VALID_TOKEN...
*** Response HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"missing required scope: inference.request"}
```

sam: can they dump the incoming request at our gateway side? request headers from envoy would confirm.

maria: attached our gateway access log snippet (sanitized):

maria: ```
[2026-03-16T22:01:12Z] "POST /v1/complete HTTP/1.1" 403 - upstream_cluster:dedicated: 
request_headers: { host: "dedicated-123.redwood.example.com", x-forwarded-for: "10.2.3.4", x-forwarded-proto: "https", content-type: "application/json" }
```

alex: interesting — Authorization header missing in the log. That points to the LB or an L7 proxy removing it. Did the NLB do any TCP to HTTP translation or a TLS offload?

maria: customer confirms the NLB does TLS termination and rewrites to internal HTTP to an Istio ingress in the VPC.

devin: classic. Some TLS terminators drop or normalize 'Authorization' when acting as a reverse proxy, or if they inject auth cookies. Also, some autoscaling proxies perform header sanitization for security.

sam: we should check: 1) whether the NLB sets proxy_protocol and passes original TLS SNI; 2) whether Istio Gateway has header normalization filters (Envoy config).

maria: asked them to check Istio ingressgateway EnvoyFilter and any ext_authz sidecar. They replied with their istio gateway config:

maria: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: redwood-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    istio: ingressgateway
  servers:
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
    tls:
      mode: SIMPLE
      credentialName: tls-secret
    hosts:
    - "dedicated-123.redwood.example.com"
```

alex: any EnvoyFilter?

maria: they have an ext_authz filter pointing to an internal SSO proxy that validates cookies and mints an opaque token. Their ext_authz logs show the incoming request to ext_authz had Authorization header blank.

devin: if the HTTPS->HTTP terminator is performing HTTP/2 multiplexing and header compression, some middlebox implementations accidentally drop 'Authorization' on connection reuse. Repro test: have them curl with --http1.1 to force HTTP/1.1 at LB and also test with a short-lived connection (Connection: close).

maria: customer ran that. With --http1.1 the request includes Authorization and returns 200. With default (http2) it's 403. They also saw the header present when doing Connection: close.

sam: that nails it — header loss with HTTP/2/on-the-wire compression or HPACK table behavior on the terminator. Might be a buggy HAProxy/NGINX/LB implementation.

alex: mitigation options: 1) ask LB vendor to fix header forwarding; 2) configure LB to preserve/forward Authorization header and not compact or re-use streams; 3) as temporary workaround, allow an alternative header mapping (e.g., X-Forwarded-Authorization or x-original-authorization) — but need to be careful security-wise.

maria: customer asks if we can accept a forwarded header name for Dedicated temporarily. Security: we'd need to ensure it's only honored from trusted LB source IPs and authenticated via mTLS or signed header.

devin: agree — if we support an alternate header, require inbound connection mTLS to the gateway from that LB IP range, and only on Dedicated/VPC deployments where customer controls LB. Also add a small audit flag to log when alt-header used.

sam: quick triage actions for us: 1) add debug logging to record if Authorization exists at TCP ingress vs after our TLS termination (we have partial visibility), 2) produce a recommended config snippet for customers to force HTTP/1.1 or Connection: close on NLB, 3) optionally offer temporary gateway mapping with strict IP allowlist + mTLS.

maria: will draft the workaround guidance and propose the alt-header flow to security for approval. For customer: asked them to flip NLB -> preserve HTTP/1.1/disable HTTP2 or test Connection: close, and we'll keep monitoring.

infra-bot: created support ticket #SUP-2026-1347 and attached logs.

maria: thanks all — I'll update when customer confirms their change. :thumbsup:
